The Game DD: an unofficial PC-88VA / PC-88VA2 port of an arcade game
(MS-DOS 4.0 disk, dd-pc88va)

This is an independent, unofficial program. It is not made, endorsed or
supported by the owners of the original game or by NEC.

The disk holds MS-DOS 4.0 for the PC-88VA (FreeDOS-88VA project, MIT
licence, see LICENSE.TXT and README.TXT on the disk) and DD.COM (two-clause
BSD licence, see DDLICENS.TXT). It contains no data from the arcade game:
you need your own copies of its ROM files. A Python script on your PC
checks them and adds the game data to the disk.

Package
-------
    dd-msdos4.d88     the disk, without game data
    DD.COM            the game (also on the disk)
    install_roms.py   adds the game data built from your ROM files
    *.py              modules used by install_roms.py; pcengine_disk.py
                      (vaeg project) writes the files to the disk
    DD.TXT            this file
    DDLICENS.TXT      the licence

Adding the game data
--------------------
You need Python 3.10 or later; for the fitted FM voices also NumPy
(pip install numpy). With the game's current commercial re-release, give
its plugin DLL, Release_0.dll (394240 bytes, CRC-32 AA58DC77, in the
Plugins folder of the game's data folder), or simply the game's install
folder; run, in this directory (on Windows, py instead of python3):

    python3 -I install_roms.py --fit-fm dd-msdos4.d88 Release_0.dll dd-msdos4-roms.d88

The ROM files themselves, in a directory or a zip file (any names), work
as well:

    python3 -I install_roms.py --fit-fm dd-msdos4.d88 ROMS.zip dd-msdos4-roms.d88

The script
  1. finds the ROMs listed below by size and CRC-32 (in the DLL, wherever
     they are stored) and checks them by SHA-1; it names the ones it does
     not find,
  2. patches the three programs and decodes the graphics into DDGAME.DAT,
  3. with --fit-fm, fits the FM voices to the sound PROM's waveforms on
     your PC (about a quarter of a minute on a fast multi-core PC; much
     longer on a slow one) into FMVOICE.DAT,
  4. adds DDGAME.DAT and FMVOICE.DAT to the root of a copy of the disk, the
     third argument (by default dd-msdos4-roms.d88), and writes
     FMVOICE.DAT beside it.

Without --fit-fm the disk has SSG sound only. Other options: --quick-fm
makes approximate FM voices at once and needs no NumPy; --fmvoice
FMVOICE.DAT reuses voices made before; --revision rev1 or rev2 chooses
the programs when the source holds both.

DD.COM only loads DDGAME.DAT and FMVOICE.DAT and the game checks them
(CRC-32) when it starts; the PC-88VA does no FM fitting. The two files can
also be copied to a disk under MS-DOS. dd-msdos4-roms.d88, DDGAME.DAT and
FMVOICE.DAT hold data from your ROMs: keep them for yourself, do not
distribute them.

ROM files
---------
Shared by both program revisions:

    size   CRC-32
    4096   A41BCE72   sound program
    2048   F14A6FE1   characters
    4096   E22957C8   sprites 1
    4096   2829EC99   sprites 2
    4096   458499E9   sprites 3
    4096   C58252A0   sprites 4
    4096   7B383983   background tiles
    4096   2CF399C2   background maps
      32   4CB9DA99   colours
     256   00C7C419   sprite colour lookup
     256   E9B3E08E   background colour lookup
     256   7A2815B4   sound waveforms

Main (4 files) and sub (2 files) programs of either revision:

    rev1       rev2
    B9198079   A80EC984   main 1
    B2ACBE49   559F00BD   main 2
    D6407B49   8CBC6FE1   main 3
    F4CEBC16   D066F830   main 4
    370EF9B4   6687933B   sub 1
    361EEB71   843D857F   sub 2

All are 4096 bytes. rev1 is the revision in the current commercial
re-release's DLL; a zip extracted from it by game-extraction-toolbox
(https://github.com/shawngmc/game-extraction-toolbox) can be given too.

Running
-------
The disk starts DD from AUTOEXEC.BAT. DD [directory] looks for DDGAME.DAT
and FMVOICE.DAT in another directory; without them it says so and returns
to MS-DOS.

The game needs a monitor that accepts 15 kHz (320x224 at 15.98 kHz), and
the machine must be started in 15 kHz mode (CRT mode: DIP switch SW1 off);
started at 24 kHz, DD stops with a message. It needs the standard 512 KB
of memory, all of it from segment 2000h up: DD must be loaded below 2000h
(MS-DOS 4.0 from this disk loads it at about 1DDCh). Picture the game with
the monitor turned clockwise: the top of the game is on the left of the
screen.

First an alignment screen is shown for about 5 seconds: let the monitor
adjust itself, move the picture with keypad 8 2 4 6 (or the cursor keys),
start at once with RETURN or SPACE. The position is kept until DD ends.

Keys (in the game's orientation):

    cursor keys, keypad 8 2 4 6   move
    SPACE, keypad 0               action
    5                             coin
    1                             start
    F10                           service screen
    F9                            load display (see below)
    ESC                           restart the machine

Service screen (F10; the game is paused): DIP switches (coins, lives,
bonus, level, continue, demo sound), SOUND (SSG, or FM when FMVOICE.DAT
was installed), TEST (20 sounds), ROUND (for testing: games start at
that round; OFF is normal play) and FPS (60, the default: the picture is
drawn every frame when there is time; 30: every second frame, lighter). Cursor keys or keypad 8 2 choose, 4 6
change (held, they repeat), RETURN or SPACE plays the sound or adds 10 to
ROUND, F10 returns.
Changed switches restart the game; they are not saved. ROUND applies from
the next game start and is kept until DD ends.

Load display (F9 turns it on and off), in the margins (above and below
the picture; on the turned monitor it reads like the game's own text),
over the last 60 frames, each number after its letter:

    F  game frames (60 at full speed)
    D  frames dropped (skipped: the game fell more than 3 frames behind)
    R  pictures drawn (60: every frame)
    T  sound ticks (120)
    I  idle time, percent
    K  (other margin, hex) the keys read
    M  (other margin, hex) the input chip's mode
    S  (other margin, hex) the sound: 01 the sound chip stopped
       answering, 02 FM voices loaded, 04 FM in use

Sound uses the YM2203: FM voices when fitted ones were installed
(--fit-fm), otherwise SSG square waves; F10 switches between them. Neither
reproduces the original waveform sound exactly.

Status: an experimental build, checked on an emulator. In busy scenes the
game can fall slightly behind the full speed. When the whole background
changes (a coin, the start of a round) it is redrawn over a few frames,
top to bottom, so that the game and its sound keep running.
